sections.label: Statutes Miscellaneous Amendments Bill
sections.summary: The Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill contains 21 clauses and makes miscellaneous amendments to several Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: (for the Minister for National Development): Mr Speaker, Sir, on behalf of the Minister for National Development, I move, "That the Bill be now read a Second time." The Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill contains 21 clauses and makes miscellaneous amendments to several Acts.

sections.label: BCA managing government programmes
sections.summary: BCA will act as the Government's agent in managing programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme and the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: BCA will act as the Government's agent in managing programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP) for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme.

sections.label: URA planning infrastructure
sections.summary: URA will undertake and coordinate the planning of infrastructure for transport, utilities and other infrastructure in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: URA will undertake and coordinate the planning of infrastructure for transport, utilities and other infrastructure in Singapore.

sections.label: Architects and Professional Engineers Acts
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 8 amend the Architects Act 1991 and Professional Engineers Act 1991 to allow the Boards to recognise pre-graduation internship and working experience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 8 will amend the Architects Act 1991 and Professional Engineers Act 1991.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: These amendments allow the Board of Architects and Professional Engineers Board to recognise relevant pre-graduation internship and working experience as part of the practical experience required for registration as Professional Engineers and Architects.

sections.label: BCA Aggregate Importer's Licence period
sections.summary: Clause 14 amends section 31(5) of the BCA Act to increase the maximum licence period from two years to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Clause 14 amends section 31(5) of the BCA Act so that the maximum licence period for BCA Aggregate Importer's Licence is increased from the current two years to five years as a pro-enterprise measure.

sections.label: HDB recovering vehicle charges
sections.summary: The amendments will expressly allow HDB to recover charges and expenses related to immobilisation, removal and storage of unlawfully parked or abandoned vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Further, the amendments will expressly allow HDB to recover charges and expenses related to the immobilisation, removal and storage of unlawfully parked or abandoned vehicles in HDB common property and open spaces.

sections.label: Wildlife feeding penalties raised
sections.summary: Clause 19 raises maximum penalties for wildlife feeding offences under section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965, with up to 12 months' imprisonment for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Clause 19 raises the maximum penalties for wildlife feeding offences under section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Further, imprisonment for a term of up to 12 months may be imposed on repeat offenders.

sections.label: Validating past HDB and URA fees
sections.summary: Clauses validate past fees and charges collected by HDB and URA, including those arising from enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On HDB-related provisions, I note the clauses validating past fees and charges collected by HDB and URA, including those arising from enforcement actions.

sections.label: Enforcement frameworks and BCA amendments
sections.summary: Speaker raises concerns about the 7 April 2026 cut-off date and welcomes clause 2 amendments placing BCA programme administration on a statutory footing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Maintaining public confidence requires enforcement frameworks that are clear, prospective and robust from the start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I am also concerned about the fairness of the cut-off date of 7 April 2026, which limits affected persons' ability to commence legal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Did the Ministry consider alternatives, such as pegging the cut-off to when charges were incurred, or providing a short grace period?

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I welcome the clause 2 amendments placing BCA's administration of programmes, such as the Estate Upgrading Programme and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme on a statutory footing.

sections.label: Expanding management fund uses
sections.summary: Expanding permitted uses of management funds to include community-building activities can strengthen social cohesion, and allowing MCSTs to engage legal services and remunerate managers reflects governance realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Expanding permitted uses of management funds to include community-building activities can strengthen social cohesion, while allowing MCSTs to engage legal services and remunerate appointed managers reflects today's governance realities.

sections.label: BCA as agent for EASE
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends section 8(1) of the Building and Construction Authority Act 1999 to confer on BCA the duty to act as agent managing the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, on Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme, clause 2 amends section 8(1) of the Building and Construction Authority Act 1999 to confer on BCA the duty "to act as an agent of the Government in managing, implementing and administering programmes, such as the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme".

sections.label: Wildlife feeding offence penalties increased
sections.summary: Clause 19 amends section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965 to increase penalties for intentionally feeding any wildlife in any place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 19 amends section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965, to "increase the penalties for an offence that relates to the intentional feeding of any wildlife in any place".

sections.label: Management fund disbursement purposes
sections.summary: Clause 16 amends section 38(3) to allow management fund monies for social, cultural, educational or sports activities and legal services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In clause 16, the amendment to section 38(3) of the Building (Strata Management) Act 2004 states that "monies from a management fund may be disbursed for the following additional purposes: (a) to organise any social, cultural, educational or sports activity, or any similar activity, that benefits all subsidiary proprietors and occupiers; (b) to engage any legal services for the management corporation".

sections.label: Authorisation of expenditures above threshold
sections.summary: Expenditures above a prescribed threshold must be authorised by ordinary or special resolution at the annual general meeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the current framework, expenditures above a prescribed threshold must be authorised through an ordinary or a special resolution at the annual general meeting, ensuring that residents have a say in significant financial decisions.

sections.label: HDB recovery from compensation
sections.summary: The clause amends sections 59, 63 and 67 to let HDB recover fees, expenses and legal costs from compensation payable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The clause in question amends sections 59, 63 and 67 of the Housing and Development Act, "enabling HDB to recover fees, expenses and legal costs from any compensation payable, whether in cases of property vesting under section 59 or compulsory acquisition under section 63".

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to figures released by MND, 203 HDB flats were compulsorily acquired between January 2020 and June 2022.

sections.label: Questions on compensation deductions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether a cap and a statutory floor will apply to deductions from compensation for affected households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, will there be a cap on the amount that may be clawed back from compensation payable to affected households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, for families who face not only mortgage arrears but other concurrent financial obligations, whether the Ministry will include a statutory floor below which compensation cannot be reduced by deductions, to ensure that no family walks away from compulsory acquisition with an amount insufficient to secure alternative housing.

sections.label: Validation of sums collected
sections.summary: Part 4 asks the House to declare sums collected by HDB, NParks, URA and the Commissioner of Building Control were validly collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Part 4 asks this House to declare that the sums collected over a period of years by four agencies under MND, namely HDB, NParks, URA and the Commissioner of Building Control were always validly collected.

sections.label: Quantum of validated sums
sections.summary: Questions ask the aggregate quantum collected under each of the four validating clauses and the period of collection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, what is the aggregate quantum of the sums being validated under Part 4?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How much money in total was collected under each of the four validating clauses and over what period?

sections.label: Cross-Government review of Part 4 discovery
sections.summary: Asks whether a cross-Government review was commissioned in response to the discovery that led to Part 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifth, has a cross-Government review been commissioned in response to the discovery that led to Part 4?

sections.label: Enhanced custodial penalty for invasive birds
sections.summary: The enhanced custodial penalty signals commitment to tackling invasive bird disamenities but may have unintended consequences for seniors and the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the enhanced custodial penalty signals the Government is committed to tackling disamenities caused by invasive bird species, it may lead to unintended consequences, especially among seniors and the vulnerable.

sections.label: Validated fees, thresholds and legal safeguards
sections.summary: Asks whether retrospectively validated fees were previously challenged or criticised, and what lessons and process improvements followed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: With clear thresholds, a graduated enforcement approach, strong social safeguards and proactive outreach, the amendment's intent can be achieved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill confirms the legality of fees collected before specified dates, while preserving the effect of existing Court decisions or ongoing proceedings and barring new lawsuits commenced after 7 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: While such validation clauses may be necessary to provide legal certainty, they should also prompt reflection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to ask the Ministry whether any of these retrospectively validated fees were previously subject of legal challenge or adverse judicial comment?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: If so, what lessons have been learned from these episodes and more broadly, what steps have been taken to strengthen internal processes and legal review, so that statutory powers to levy fees and charges are consistently clear, properly authorised and transparent going forward?

sections.label: BCA role in private residential estates
sections.summary: The Bill allows BCA to act as a government agent managing and administering programmes upgrading public spaces and facilities in private residential estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My first point, it is about the expanded role of BCA in private residential estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill allows BCA to act as an agent of a government in managing, implementing and administering programme for upgrading of public spaces, infrastructure and facilities in private residential estates.

sections.label: BCA support to professional boards
sections.summary: Questions whether building made life meaningfully better, and notes the Bill lets BCA provide administrative support to the professional engineer and strata title boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In other words, the question should not be, "Did we build something?" but it should be "Did we make life meaningfully better for our residents as a result of all these things that we are building?" My second point concerns about the Bill's provision of BCA to provide administrative support services to bodies of the professional engineer board and strata title board.

sections.label: URA coordinating transport and infrastructure planning
sections.summary: Asks whether URA's clearer coordinating role will help agencies systematically identify accessibility gaps such as overhead bridges without lifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: An overhead bridge, without lift access, can be a real obstacle, especially in our mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, when URA takes a clearer coordinating role in transport and infrastructure planning, will this help agencies, including LTA, where relevant, identify, prioritise such accessibility gaps more systematically, including overhead bridges without lifts?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If URA's role is to coordinate the planning of transport, utilities and other infrastructures, then I hope the coordination will be felt not just in master plans or major development, but also in the small practical improvements that affect daily lives.

sections.label: Pre-qualification of practical experience
sections.summary: The speaker's fourth point concerns recognising pre-qualification of practical experience for architects and professional engineers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My fourth point concerns recognising pre-qualification of practical experience for architects and professional engineers.

sections.label: Architects and engineers safety standards
sections.summary: Architects and professional engineers affect building infrastructure and public safety, so flexible pathways must not dilute standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Because architects and professional engineers make decisions that will affect building infrastructure and safety of our public.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, while we make pathways more flexible, we must be careful that we do not dilute standards.

sections.label: Unknowingly breaking law on species
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government will ensure ordinary individuals do not unknowingly break the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, they may not know its origin, whether it is derived from a regulated species.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Government – how will the Government ensure that ordinary individuals do not unknowingly break the law?

sections.label: Views validate agency fees and charges
sections.summary: The views validate various fees and charges previously collected by BCA, HDB, NParks and URA.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The views validate various fees and charges previously collected by agencies as BCA, HDB, NParks and URA.

sections.label: Extinguishing rights to challenge collections
sections.summary: Parliament is asked to validate past collections and extinguish rights to challenge them in court for those who had not commenced proceedings before 7 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is not unremarkable is the full scope of what Parliament is being asked to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are not simply being asked to validate past collections, we are also being asked to simultaneously extinguish citizens' rights to challenge those collections in court – permanently – for anyone who had not commenced proceedings before 7 April 2026, the date of the First Reading of this Bill.

sections.label: Missing details on four agencies
sections.summary: Parliament has not been given the duration of the lapse, amounts collected or deducted, or how many individuals were affected for the four agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For each of the four agencies in Part 4 – BCA, HDB, NParks and URA – Parliament has not been given the duration of the lapse, the total amounts collected, or deducted without authority, or any account of how many individuals were affected and to what extent.

sections.label: Deductions and past legal challenge
sections.summary: Clause 18 prospectively authorises deductions, while Part 4 declares past deductions lawful and blocks legal challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 18 prospectively authorises that deductions going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But Part 4 simultaneously declares that past deductions were always lawful and closes the door on any legal challenge.

sections.label: Workers' Party on correcting errors
sections.summary: The Workers' Party says errors can be corrected but legislative power should not erase past wrongs or remove citizens' right to justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party recognises that administrative errors made by Government agencies can be corrected, but the way to correct a mistake should not be to use legislative power to wipe the slate clean on past wrongdoings or worse, to strip ordinary citizens of their right to seek justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It must clearly state how many people have been affected by this error and the total sum involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It should also explain why it is not considering refunding the fees that were wrongly collected.

sections.label: Extinguishing rights without information
sections.summary: Parliament is asked to extinguish legal rights without information on who was affected, by how much, or why refunds were not considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Parliament is being asked to extinguish citizens' legal rights without being given the basic information to assess whether that is appropriate, who was affected, by how much and why restitution, that is, refunds to the affected individuals, especially those whose flats have been compulsorily acquired, was not considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government's own standard, set as recently as 2024, requires more than this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These are the clearer mandates for the BCA and URA, the provisions that enable Government-funded upgrading in private residential estates, and the formal certification framework for endangered species under our environmental laws.

sections.label: New BCA and URA functions
sections.summary: The amendments give BCA new statutory functions for private estate upgrading and expand URA's mandate to coordinate infrastructure planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendments confer new statutory functions on BCA as the Government agency for upgrading programmes in private residential estates and expand URA's statutory mandate to coordinate not just land use but transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning.

sections.label: Upgrading private residential estates
sections.summary: Clearer statutory powers extend Government-driven upgrading to private residential estates, recognising environmental quality matters for social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By giving clearer statutory powers for Government-driven upgrading programmes to extend to private residential estates, we recognise that the quality of the environment in these neighbourhoods also matters for social cohesion and inclusion.

sections.label: Certification for endangered species
sections.summary: The speaker strongly supports provisions that formalise certification for endangered species and related products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Third, I strongly support the provisions that formalise certification for endangered species and related products.

sections.label: Clearer certification framework for hybrid plants
sections.summary: A clearer certification framework, including for hybrid plants or products from scheduled species, gives traders, travellers and enforcement agencies a common understanding of the rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A clearer certification framework, including for hybrid plants or products derived from scheduled species, gives traders, travellers and enforcement agencies a common understanding of the rules.

sections.label: Updated penalty framework for wildlife crimes
sections.summary: The amendment updates the penalty framework, solidifies the stance on wildlife feeding and strengthens enforcement, sending a message that wildlife crimes are serious harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our current penalty framework has not been updated in decades and no longer reflects the seriousness with which we treat wildlife crimes or the subtle ways we harm the ecosystem through our actions, no matter how well-intentioned they may be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With this amendment, we solidify our stance on wildlife feeding and strengthen enforcement, sending a clear message – wildlife crimes are serious harms.

sections.label: Artificial feeding disrupts ecosystem
sections.summary: Artificial feeding can disrupt the ecosystem, leading to increased competition with native birds and eventually culling in massive numbers when populations affect the human environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Artificial feeding can disrupt the ecosystem, leading to increased competition with native birds and eventually culling in massive numbers when populations start to affect our human environment.

sections.label: Alternative penalties for illegal bird feeding
sections.summary: A CNA report stated nearly 320 illegal bird feeding cases this year, half involving seniors, and asked if Government would consider alternative penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A CNA report on 17 March this year stated that, on average, there were nearly 320 cases of illegal bird feeding this year, with half of them involving seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider alternative forms of penalty for repeat offenders, such as corrective community service alongside psychological and social support?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is crucial since illegal feeding often reflects a deeper issue: an epidemic of senior loneliness.

sections.label: CNA report on illegal bird-feeding
sections.summary: A CNA report on 17 March this year stated there were nearly 320 cases of illegal bird-feeding a year, with half involving seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   A CNA report on 17 March this year stated that, on average, there were nearly 320 cases of illegal bird-feeding a year, with half of them involving seniors.

sections.label: URA's infrastructure coordination role
sections.summary: URA coordinates and resolves differences in priorities and timelines across projects, and the amendments formally recognise its role and give it a clear mandate to coordinate infrastructure planning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: URA's role here is to coordinate and resolve differences in priorities and timelines across different projects to ensure quality infrastructure can be delivered in an optimised way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Therefore, what the amendments seek to do is to formally recognise URA's role and give it a clear mandate to coordinate the planning of infrastructure.

sections.label: BCA manages private estate upgrading
sections.summary: BCA will manage infrastructure upgrading projects in private residential estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: BCA will manage infrastructure upgrading projects in private residential estates.

sections.label: EASE Private contractor appointments
sections.summary: BCA appoints contractors to install senior-friendly fittings for eligible seniors to improve mobility and safety at home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: To Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik's question about the EASE (Private) programme, I wish to clarify that BCA appoints the contractors to install the senior-friendly fittings for eligible seniors to improve mobility and safety within their homes.

sections.label: BCA back-office support to boards
sections.summary: BCA provides routine back-office administrative support to the Professional Engineers Board Singapore and the Strata Titles Boards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: BCA provides routine back-office administrative support to the Professional Engineers Board Singapore and the Strata Titles Boards, such as in book-keeping and payroll processing.

sections.label: Fees not prescribed in legislation
sections.summary: Fees were not formally prescribed in legislation as they were first regarded as administrative charges; a 2025 MND review advised legislating them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: The policy intent is clear and consistent with cost recovery principles, but the fees were not formally prescribed in subsidiary legislation or the parent Act at the time of implementation, as they were first regarded as administrative charges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Upon a 2025 review conducted by MND, in consultation with the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), MND was advised that it is better for these identified fees to be provided for in legislation.

sections.label: Fees appropriate and being validated
sections.summary: The fees charged were appropriate and not wrongly collected, and validation is ongoing to align with legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: The fees charged were appropriate, not wrongly collected and we are validating to ensure that this is, moving forward, aligned with legislation.

sections.label: Fee validation date for queries
sections.summary: The fees are validated up to the date they are regularised, not 7 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: On Ms Valerie Lee and Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim's queries, the fees are validated up to the date on which the fees are regularised and not 7 April 2026.

sections.label: Reenacted strata management amendments
sections.summary: The amendments were already passed under the Building Maintenance and Strata Management (Amendment) Act 2017 and introduce no new policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: To clarify, the present amendments that are part of the Bill had already been passed under the Building Maintenance and Strata Management (Amendment) Act 2017, and do not introduce new policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: The amendments reenact these provisions, moving them into the Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill to facilitate staged commencement.

sections.label: Questions on fees collected
sections.summary: The speaker asks how much money was collected under each of the four validating clauses, over what period, and how many Singaporeans were affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: And again, these are things, like paying to expedite a TOP application, paying to register a renovation contractor, so I hope the Ministry understands why it is, one, important to get a sense of the numbers, both in the sense of the total amounts that need to be claimed and the total amount of people affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: So, I would like to reiterate the questions that I have asked: how much money in total was collected under each of the four validating clauses and over what period?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: How many Singaporeans have been affected by these collections?

sections.label: Validating past fee collections
sections.summary: Fees were charged on a cost recovery basis, and the Bill validates past collections and gives agencies legislative backing to promulgate fees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: And in the course of providing these services, they had expended additional resources to deliver the services to the end user, manpower cost, administrative cost, system cost, with a view towards delivering services for the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: And on top of that, these fees were charged on the basis of cost recovery for the provision of such services, and as I have mentioned earlier in my Opening Speech as well as the Round-up Speech, that the review was conducted by the Ministry in 2025 in consultation with AGC, and it was advised that it is better for the fees charged for carrying statutory and regulatory functions to be provided for in legislation, which is what we are doing today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: So, the framing of what Mr Fadli is saying that it is something that we are trying to claim back or claw back, it is not the right framing for which we are actually moving this Bill forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: And essentially, it seeks to validate past collections of the same identified fees, which then further ensures that the fees are then subsequently legislated, the agencies are given the legislative backing to further promulgate these fees and going forward, the fees will be regularised through subsidiary legislation under relevant parent Acts.

sections.label: Questions on illegal collection and refunds
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the fees were illegally collected and whether there will be refunds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: Now the Senior Parliamentary Secretary is using a number of different terms: "duly", "appropriate", "not wrongly collected", "good faith".

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I think the simple question is: were the fees illegally collected?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: So, perhaps, if the Senior Parliamentary Secretary could clarify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: And finally, it is a very simple question: will there be refunds?

sections.label: HDB fees range
sections.summary: HDB fees range from $3.27 for renewing an HDB Fire Insurance policy to $545 for consent to sell a commercial property.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: In terms of the fees charged by HDB, the fees range from $3.27 for the renewal of a policy under the HDB Fire Insurance scheme for owners who default in renewing the policy, to $545 for an application for HDB's consent to sell a commercial property not under the lodgement scheme.

sections.label: Fees collected since Independence
sections.summary: The fees were collected over a long period of time, since Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Because we have been — Yes, Minister Chee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is that I hope they understand, these fees were collected over a long period of time – if I am not wrong, I think, since Independence when we first started.

sections.label: Order of magnitude of fees
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Government can give an order of magnitude for the number of fees collected and the total quantum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand the difficulty in getting the exact numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But is there an order of magnitude that the Government can provide as to how many such fees were collected and what is the total quantum?

sections.label: Window for claimants to claim
sections.summary: The member asks if a window of time will be given for claimants, but the Government says the fees were not wrongly collected and need not be refunded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And is Government prepared to provide at least a window of time for the claimants to make a claim for these fees which were not correctly collected?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I have explained earlier that these fees were not illegally or wrongly collected, and they were not inappropriately collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We were trying to recover the costs for providing these services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is not a wrong collection that we are required to refund or we should refund.

sections.label: Risk of oversight in claims
sections.summary: The member says there is a real risk of oversight given the amount and people involved, and claims should not be extinguished with finality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: Because my concern is that there is a real risk of oversight due to the amount and people involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: We should not have such a finality of extinguishing their claims.

sections.label: Validating past collections via Bill
sections.summary: The fees were previously treated as administrative, will now be put into legislation, and the Bill seeks Parliament's agreement to validate past collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Today, we are here because the nature in which these fees were prescribed, they were treated as administrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But going forward, we will put them into legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And then there is this issue of what to do with the past collections, which we are proposing through this Bill, for Parliament's agreement, to validate.

sections.label: Past collections were not authorised
sections.summary: The past collections were not authorised, which is why AGC said they should have been prescribed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The fact of the matter is that those past collections were not authorised, and that is why AGC has said that they should have been prescribed.

sections.label: AGC advice on past collections
sections.summary: The member asks whether AGC advised that pre-First Reading collections were illegal, and the Government says AGC advised putting the fees into legislation going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Was MND advised, after the review with AGC, was it the AGC's position that collections before the First Reading of the Bill were illegal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But AGC also supported – we would not be able to present this Bill if it is not with the support of the AGC – that we come to Parliament and seek Parliament's approval for the Bill to validate the past collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Was it the AGC's position that the collections hitherto were illegal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I have explained this earlier, Mr Speaker, that AGC's advice to us was that these fees, because we considered them as administrative, it is better going forward from a legal point of view to put them into the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The way in which we address this is to bring the Bill before the House in an open manner and to explain to the House this is what happened, this is what we are proposing, and to validate these past collections.

sections.label: Fees in legislation
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for whole House support and says fees will be part of the legislation going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I hope, as I said, to be able to get the support from the whole House in terms of how we deal with this so that we can move forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But going forward, the fees will be part of the legislation.

sections.label: Dissent recorded, Ayes have it
sections.summary: The Speaker asks those wanting their dissent recorded to stand, then says the Ayes have it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Could those who want to have their dissent recorded, please stand?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I think the "Ayes" have it, the "Ayes" have it.    .
